header: PROBABLE PF AT SUPERANNUATION, WORKED OUT FROM THE DSP PROVIDENT FUND PAGE AND THE PAYSLIP. An employee of DSP can see only these figures: on the PF page of the legacy intranet (Provident Fund Statement of the financial year: the opening balance, the interest on it, the monthly contributions so far, the interest on them and the closing balance, each for PF (Emp), PF (Comp) and V.P.F), on the yearly PF statement (the taxable balance) and on the payslip (the monthly PF and VPF). My calculator takes exactly those figures and carries them forward month by month to the retirement date. It is a pure function: the numbers a person types are used in the browser and are never stored, logged or sent anywhere. THE METHOD IS THE PF TRUST'S OWN, read from a DSP yearly statement (the sums were checked against every line of one: the interest on the opening balance, on the monthly contributions, the taxable part, the TDS and the closing balance):
* Interest on the OPENING balance of a year = opening x rate x months / 12 (a whole year: opening x rate).

* Interest on a MONTH'S CONTRIBUTION runs from the month of the contribution itself: April's earns 12 months of the year, March's earns 1 month (so a month's interest is worked out on the running balance INCLUDING that month's contribution). It is not compounded within the year; the interest is added to the balance at the end of the year (31 March) or at retirement.
* The company's share in the PF account = the employee's 12% less the pension part (EPS, Rs 1,250 a month: 8.33% of Rs 15,000).

* TAXABLE INTEREST: what the employee puts in (PF and VPF together) beyond Rs 2,50,000 in a financial year is taxable, and so is the interest on it and on the taxable balance carried from earlier years. The trust deducts 10% TDS on that interest from the employee's column when the year is closed (the rest of the income tax is recovered from the pay and is not part of the PF).

These are APPROXIMATIONS and the screen says so: the rate of each future year is declared later, and pay, DA and increments change. I made every rate and limit an input with a default, not a hidden constant.

members.name: postedMonth
doc: The month and year the PF page says "Monthly Recovery Posted upto" (10 and 2026 for "10/2026 Paybill").

members.name: retireMonth
doc: The retirement date's month and year (March 2032 for 30 March 2032).

members.name: opening
doc: (a) opening balance as on 1 April, from the PF page.

members.name: contributions
doc: (e) the monthly contributions of the current financial year so far, from the PF page.

members.name: contributionInterest
doc: (f) the interest on those monthly contributions so far, from the PF page.

members.name: interestPct
doc: The yearly rate in percent for the months still to come (the page's own rate, 8.25, until a new one is declared).

members.name: pageRatePct
doc: The rate the page used for the months already posted (the page prints it: "Interest Rate : 8.25%"). It does not change when you try another rate for the future.

members.name: monthlyEmp
doc: The employee's monthly PF as the payslip prints it (CPF PC).

members.name: epsPart
doc: The pension part taken out of the company's share each month (1,250).

members.name: monthlyVpf
doc: The VPF you will pay each month from now, in rupees, and the ceiling on it (30,000 a month).

members.name: risePct
doc: A yearly rise in the PF wage (basic + DA), in percent, applied from the next April; I leave the rest of this year at today's figure.

members.name: taxableOpening
doc: The taxable balance of the last yearly statement ("TAXBL CB"), or null if you do not have it; then I take no tax on interest off.

members.name: taxFreeLimit
doc: What the employee may put in before interest turns taxable (2,50,000 a year) and the TDS the trust deducts (10%).

members.name: months
doc: The months of this year that are carried (12, or fewer in the first year and in the retirement year).

members.name: added
doc: The contributions added in this year (from now, in the first year).

members.name: interest
doc: The interest of the whole year, and the TDS taken off it.

members.name: closing
doc: The balance at the close of the year (or on retirement).

members.name: now
doc: The balance as the PF page shows it now: a + b + e + f (b = a x rate x months / 12).

members.name: postedMonths
doc: The months already posted in the current year, and the months still to come until retirement.

members.name: futureContributions
doc: From now to retirement: what is added by contributions and by interest (before TDS), and the TDS.

members.name: taxableClosing
doc: The taxable balance at retirement, if the opening one was given.

symbols.name: PF_DEFAULTS
symbols.sig: const PF_DEFAULTS = { interestPct: 8.25, pageRatePct: 8.25, epsPart: 1250, vpfCeiling: 30000, monthlyVpf: 30000, risePct: 5, taxFreeLimit: 2 …
doc: What the form starts with: figures the PF trust and the Company publish, not the person's own.

behaviours: a month's place in the financial year: April 1 ... March 12; the year of January 2027 is 2026-27
the month and the date are read as typed (10/2026, 30/03/2032) and refused when impossible
one whole year (eleven months after April): the employee column is 1,205,200 (opening + 12 months + interest on the opening balance + interest from each month's own month)
the company's share is the employee's CPF less the pension part (10,000 - 1,250 = 8,750 a month): 500,000 + 105,000 + 40,000 + 4,550
the voluntary part: none gives only the opening balance and its interest (200,000 + 16,000)
a monthly VPF of 30,000 adds 360,000 and 30,000 x 8% x 6.5 = 15,600 of interest
a VPF above the ceiling is cut to the ceiling (50,000 is taken as 30,000)
the parts add up: the closing balance = opening + added + interest (- TDS)
where the page stands now: a + a x 8% x 7/12 + e + f for each column
to the end of the year: the page's interest on the posted months, the posted months' remaining months, and each coming month from its own month
five months are still to be paid, and 50,000 + 43,750 are added by the employee and the company
five years: five rows, 2026-27 to 2030-31, each 12 months
the first coming year stays at today's CPF and the pay rise starts the April after (10,000, 10,500, 11,025)
each year closes at the last year's close + what was added + the interest - the TDS
a retirement inside the year: only the months up to the retirement month, interest for those months (40,000 + 1,400)
another rate for the future leaves the page's own interest on the posted months alone (the balance now is the page's, whatever rate is tried)
a higher rate, a higher rise and a longer career each give more
the taxable part: 110,000 beyond the limit, interest 1,733.33, TDS 173.33, taxable balance 111,560
the TDS is taken from the employee's column only, and the other columns are as without tax
a taxable balance carried in earns taxable interest too: 100,000 at 8% adds 8,000 of taxable interest and 800 of TDS
under the limit nothing is taxable: 10,000 a month (120,000 in a year) and no taxable balance gives no TDS
with no taxable balance given, no TDS is taken off and the result says so (taxableClosing is null)
the months of the page already posted count as equal parts of what the page shows: 436,920 posted in 7 months crosses the limit
the what-if table has a row for each rise and a cell for each rate, and a higher rate or rise gives a higher figure
impossible inputs are told, never worked out
the defaults are the published ones: 8.25% rate, EPS part 1,250, VPF ceiling 30,000, limit 2,50,000, TDS 10%
